module purpose: neorv32_debug_dm implements a debug-module register file and abstract-command sequencer. It accepts DMI requests and debug-bus accesses, stores control, command, program-buffer and data-register state, generates halt and reset requests for selected harts, reports debug status/data, and can gate these operations through an optional authenticator.

use-case flows.value: debug-module control settings: dmactive, ndmreset, halt request, resume request, reset acknowledge, and selected hart
abstract command, autoexec configuration, program buffer entries, and debug data register writes
abstract command start decision from a command write or an autoexec-triggering data0/progbuf access
abstract command validation, helper-instruction preparation, execution trigger, busy tracking, and CPU program-buffer composition
DMI readback of debug status, control, hart information, abstract-command status, autoexec settings, data0, authenticator data, and halt summary
debug-bus reads of code ROM, composed CPU program buffer, data register, and request bits
authentication validity gating debug reads, writes, halt/reset outputs, and authenticator access when AUTHENTICATOR is enabled
asynchronous reset clears controller, status, register-file and bus/DMI response state; dmactive low also forces the command controller back to idle

conceptual assets.reasoning: In AUTHENTICATOR builds, auth.valid is delivered by the authenticator sub-unit at line 745 and gates authenticated write/read enables at lines 212-213, halt output generation at line 500, reset output generation at line 505, and most DMI status/data returns at lines 530, 555, 573, 584, 596, 604 and 614. Corrupting this decision would violate the module's implemented access-qualification rules. In not-AUTHENTICATOR builds, lines 753-754 force auth.valid to 1, so this concept is build-dependent.

dm_reg.dmcontrol_dmactive is written from the dmcontrol register at line 433 under line 424/432 decoding. When it is 0, the command controller is forced back to idle and cleared at lines 229-236; it also participates in halt_req_o at line 500, ndmrstn_o at line 505, and drives the authenticator enable input at line 743. The module's command execution, halt and reset behavior therefore depends on the integrity of this stored setting. Availability is also established because the value is held in a register and read back at line 569.

The selected hart index is stored at line 429, decoded into a one-hot target mask at line 487, and checked for in-range validity against NUM_HARTS at line 489. This setting determines which hart receives halt requests at line 500, which hart is targeted by abstract-command execution requests at line 298, which hart status bits are reported at lines 534-545, and which hart's halted state is accepted in command checking at line 266. Integrity of the target selection is therefore established.

The halt request bit is stored at line 426 and is combined with the selected-hart decode, dmactive, and authentication validity to drive halt_req_o at line 500. If this value is corrupted, the implemented halt-request flow to the targeted hart becomes incorrect. Availability is also established because the request is stored until rewritten and is exported continuously through halt_req_o under the RTL-visible conditions at line 500.

The ndmreset control bit is stored at line 430 and drives ndmrstn_o low only when dmactive is 1 and authentication is valid at line 505. The same stored bit also controls per-hart reset-related status updates at lines 355, 364, 373 and 382, and is reported back at lines 540-541 and 567. Corrupting this setting would therefore break the reset-request flow and the related status behavior. Availability is established by the held register and the continuous output rule at line 505.

dm_reg.command is accepted only when addr_command is written, authentication passes, the controller is not busy, and cmderr is 000 at lines 438-439. CMD_CHECK then validates its fields at lines 261-265, and CMD_PREPARE uses its bits to build load/store helper instructions and to enable the program buffer at lines 279-293. Corruption would change whether the command is accepted, rejected, or turned into the wrong execution sequence. Availability is established because the command is stored and then read by the controller logic in this entity.

The abstractauto settings are stored at lines 444-446. These bits directly control whether writes to data0/progbuf assert autoexec_wr at lines 450-455 and whether reads assert autoexec_rd at lines 635-641; either event can restart command checking from IDLE at lines 255-256. The exact settings therefore determine whether ordinary data/program-buffer accesses implicitly start command execution. Availability is also established because the stored settings are returned at lines 597-599.

conceptual assets.concept: Instruction sequence presented for abstract command execution
conceptual assets.reasoning: Program-buffer entries are stored at lines 465 and 470. The controller prepares the helper instruction word at lines 281-288 and 291, and cpu_progbuf is then composed as word 0 from that helper at line 508, words 1 and 2 from NOP or stored progbuf entries under pbuf_en at lines 509-510, and word 3 as a fixed ebreak at line 511. Bus reads return cpu_progbuf at line 694. Integrity is established because the bus-side consumer must receive exactly the instruction sequence defined by these lines for abstract command execution. Availability is established because the stored entries are held and the composed buffer is always formed for bus reads.

conceptual assets.concept: Abstract command execution state and busy decision
conceptual assets.reasoning: dm_ctrl.state is reset to IDLE at lines 221 and 230 and transitions through CHECK, PREPARE, TRIGGER, BUSY and ERROR at lines 252, 256, 267, 270, 274, 294, 300, 306, 311 and 315. dm_ctrl.busy is derived from state at line 339 and then blocks command, abstractauto, progbuf and data0 writes at lines 438, 443, 464, 469 and 495, and is reported at line 587. The implemented sequencing of abstract commands therefore depends on the integrity of this stored state and its derived busy decision. Availability is established because the state is held across cycles and busy is recomputed from it.

dm_ctrl.cmderr is initialized/cleared to 000 at lines 227, 236 and 331, and set to distinct codes for illegal state, exception, illegal command, or access error at lines 321-328. A nonzero error prevents a new command write from being accepted at line 438, and the code is reported in abstractcs at line 589. The correctness of both command acceptance and reported error state therefore depends on the integrity of cmderr. Availability is established because the code remains stored until explicitly cleared through the abstractcs write at lines 459-460 and 330-331.

dci.data_reg is written from an authenticated DMI data0 write at lines 495 and 665-666, or from a bus-side write to the data window at lines 667-668. The stored value is returned on DMI reads at line 605 and on bus reads at line 696. Under the module-level assumption for unsupplied consumers, integrity is established because the reader must receive exactly the transferred value defined by these write and read rules. Availability is also established because the register retains its contents until overwritten or reset.

dm_ctrl.hart_halted is cleared by ndmreset at line 356, set by a halt acknowledgement at line 358, and cleared by a resume acknowledgement at line 360. This stored status is used in CMD_CHECK to decide whether a selected hart may execute the requested abstract command at lines 266-267, and it is reported at lines 542-545 and 615. Corruption would therefore break both command qualification and reported halt status. Availability is established because the status is held per hart until updated by the defined events.

dm_ctrl.hart_resume_ack is cleared by ndmreset at line 374, set by a resume acknowledgement at line 376, and cleared again when a new selected resume request is issued at line 378. The module reports this stored status in dmstatus at lines 536-537. Integrity is established because the reported acknowledgement state must match these update rules. Availability is established because the status is retained until the next defined update.

dm_ctrl.hart_reset is set when dmcontrol_ndmreset is asserted at line 383 and cleared when a selected reset acknowledgement is written at line 385. The stored status is reported in dmstatus at lines 534-535. Integrity is established because the externally reported reset state must follow exactly these update conditions. Availability is established because the bit stays set until the defined acknowledge event clears it.
